questions.question: Explain how to determine the effect on the accounting equation of any CRJ entry, and classify the effect of entries in these sundry accounts: capital, rent income, interest income, loan, debtors control.
questions.expected_answer: Every CRJ entry debits bank, so assets increase. The credit decides the rest: current income column — OE increases (income). Sundry: capital — OE increases (capital contribution); rent income and interest income — OE increases (income); loan — liabilities increase, OE unchanged; debtors control — another asset decreases (assets +/−), OE and L unchanged.

questions.question: The April CRJ shows: bank R31 330; current income R18 650; sundry: capital R10 000, rent income R2 500, interest income R180. Summarise the month's effect on A, OE and L, and separate capital from income.
questions.expected_answer: A +R31 330. OE +R31 330 (18 650 + 10 000 + 2 500 + 180). L 0. Equation balances. Of the OE increase, capital = R10 000 and income = 18 650 + 2 500 + 180 = R21 330.

questions.question: Complete the analysis for: rent R2 500; loan R20 000; CRR R4 000; additional capital R8 000; debtor pays R1 200. Give the account debited and credited, the effect on A, OE and L, and the totals.
questions.expected_answer: Rent: Dr Bank, Cr Rent income; A +2 500, OE +2 500 (income). Loan: Dr Bank, Cr Loan; A +20 000, L +20 000. CRR: Dr Bank, Cr Current income; A +4 000, OE +4 000 (income). Capital: Dr Bank, Cr Capital; A +8 000, OE +8 000 (capital contribution). Debtor: Dr Bank, Cr Debtors control; A +1 200 and −1 200. Totals: net A +34 500; OE +14 500; L +20 000; 14 500 + 20 000 = 34 500.
